title: Go Unified Policy Authoring: persistent content and canonical source digest synchronization

responsibility_boundaries.current_work_unit: Go Authoring content+digest synchronization; no CI transport migration

work_units.name: Go policy contract module reorganization and authorized policy content/digest update
inputs: current effective developer policy and explicitly authorized policy-change input
outputs: Move existing policy contract selection, check and create responsibilities to policy/contract/entry, check and authoring; implement new update package at policy/contract/update. Rewire existing CLI and consumers to the new Go packages.
Go Authoring supports a separate explicit update operation for existing registered Unified Policy documents; existing create/check behavior remains unchanged
Authorized policy content change and its regenerated canonical source SHA-256 are materialized as one atomic file update with stale-input protection
Independent Go source-integrity/identity/lifecycle/rule-reference validation of the updated policy before commit and after materialization
Go regression evidence for both policy planes and the SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH recurrence scenario; no Python helper added
New tests for all four policy contract responsibilities are authored under developer/tests/policy/contract/ only; existing tests are relocated in the separately derived plan.
exact_steps: Inventory Go packages, exported and unexported functions, CLI entrypoints, actual callers, indexes, workflows and tests of existing contract authoring/entry/check modules; determine ownership from actual behavior, not filenames. Keep non-policy responsibility/profile behavior separate.

Resolve exact document, declared policy identity, policy kind, Family, selected Unified Policy contract, applicable current governance and authorized change scope; do not infer mutation authority from valid schema, plan status, or path name.

Relocate existing policy contract responsibilities to the four exact user-selected directories. entry owns selection; check owns read-only validation; authoring owns non-overwriting creation and serialization; update is the new explicit existing-document mutation and digest-sync owner. Avoid duplicate implementation, import cycles and reverse dependencies from common source to developer tooling.

Preserve check as read-only and generate/create as non-overwriting. Add an explicit existing-policy update path in policy/contract/update rather than changing WriteDocument's O_EXCL creation semantics.

Require an exact baseline revision or content precondition and explicit authorization for the proposed policy-content delta; reject unauthorized direct rewrites, cross-plane output paths, conflicting authority and stale concurrent input.

Share the existing Go canonical source reconstruction and source.Digest implementation: derive source from Policy_Content.items without treating the old stored digest as the new value; avoid raw YAML file hashing, duplicate digest algorithms and Python computation.

For a previously valid baseline, apply only the authorized policy delta, regenerate Policy_Content.source_document.sha256 from the reconstructed content, and validate the complete resulting Unified Policy with the existing registered verifier; reject invalid source pointers, incomplete rules, changed identity/lifecycle without authorization, and invalid bindings.

Write the approved content and computed digest together using an atomic, crash-conscious, same-directory replacement that works on Windows 11 and CI; preserve unrelated fields and report exactly which policy fields and source digest changed.

Reread the written policy and independently verify current SHA-256, source reconstruction, declared references, and unchanged unauthorized fields; fail closed and preserve or safely recover the prior valid file when materialization or readback validation fails.

Handle already-mismatched historical policies through a separately authorized, evidence-backed repair/reconciliation path; never silently accept a preexisting SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH, never rewrite an unapproved policy solely to make CI green, and do not bypass source integrity verification.

Add Go tests under developer/tests/policy/contract/ (not under .ptsip) for create versus update, successful same-document mutation plus digest synchronization, no-op stability, repeated updates, both policy planes, stale base revision, concurrent file changes, unauthorized deltas, partial/failed writes, and repair authorization boundary.

Run developer Go authoring and common source contract tests plus the registered policy check against updated fixtures. Treat Go-only replacement of changed.py in policy-contract-guard.yml as a separate verification-migration responsibility, not as the digest authoring implementation.

Update .ptsip/engine/developer/main.go and applicable developer package indexes, imports and Go command routes to the new ownership locations; validate Responsibility-Authority and all other real callers, and retire old policy-specific paths only after consumer and regression equivalence. Rewire affected test execution with developer/tests and coordinate existing test relocation without duplicating tests.
acceptance: Authorized changes to an existing Unified Policy can be performed through Go Authoring without manual source_document.sha256 editing.
The persisted SHA-256 exactly matches the existing source.Digest canonical digest for the reconstructed Policy_Content.items source and remains independently verifiable after readback.

When content is changed and the corresponding digest is stale, SOURCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH is still rejected by read-only verification; an update is accepted only through the explicit authorized mutation path.
No policy-body-only write, digest-only write, silent auto-rehash of unapproved content, or partial replacement is reported as successful.
Existing new-file create semantics, both policy planes, policy authority boundaries, and product Policy v4 source_document removal remain unchanged.
Go tests demonstrate that changes like the 2026-11-22 SFP-CNTR-0005 update are synchronized when made through authorized Go Authoring; historical mismatches are not silently normalized.
Four user-selected Go package locations exist and each owns its specified responsibility; no new _test.go under .ptsip; no stale active imports to retired policy-specific implementations.
work_units.current_result: 2026-11-23: existing Go runUnifiedAuthoring validates supplied digest before writing, and WriteDocument does not update existing files; no persistent authorized content+digest synchronization is implemented in the current authoring path.
